Accepted candidate: `7f241bbafb6a4c288e1f4ef6c6e43ecc9ebbc96b`, based on `79f970a150826ea14d9c9f6fb2f86eb2804a4ace`. The clean candidate was fast-forward integrated locally; no remote publication occurred.

F3-01 through F3-04 are accepted against the implementation report and provider compatibility evidence. The implementer observed the final assembled 242-test/typecheck/build/packed-CLI gate. Subsequent candidate changes were construction and evidence records, not runtime changes.

The manager read the fresh Codex ACCEPTED review, independently matched its recovered plan, counter, verifier and review hashes, and reran the actual verifier with exit 0. Review SHA-256: `332b5b7be0f0f5f8f64bfce9691cbdf99fa7939bd4ce0761f401c8425d9e5f31`. The earlier CHANGES REQUIRED result remains preserved; recovery did not retroactively change it. This does not claim isolated Claude/Cursor execution; the documented profile limitations remain. Independent boundary findings were remediated with focused negative evidence for prompt binding, recursive handoff schemas, worker identity/exit and orphaned admission ownership.

Efficiency lesson: consume complete persisted artifacts, never bounded diagnostic summaries. Check harness prerequisites before inference; retain successful provider work through downstream repairs. Terra capacity failure required bounded Sol-medium recovery. Phase estimates remain advisory; the owner's remaining account allowance is binding and may not be converted into an invented native token cap. Missing or overlapping telemetry remains explicitly unknown in the phase report.

Phase 4 may start from this accepted source after its brief and resource snapshot are recorded. This is phase acceptance, not V1 release acceptance.
